questions.question: Five people A, B, C, D, E are ranked in marks. Only two people scored more than B. D scored less than only A. C scored less than B and more than E. Who ranked third?
questions.title: Ranking puzzle — who is 3rd

sections.label: Given
sections.content:
Only 2 people scored more than B → B is ranked 3rd. D scored less than only A → D is ranked 2nd (A is 1st). C is less than B, more than E → among the remaining 4th/5th spots, C is 4th and E is 5th.
**Ranks:** 1-A, 2-D, 3-B, 4-C, 5-E.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: B is ranked 3rd.

questions.question: A man walks 5 km towards South, turns left and walks 3 km, then turns right and walks 4 km. In which direction is he now with respect to his starting point?
questions.title: Direction puzzle

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
Start (0,0). Walk 5 km South → (0,−5). Turn left (facing South, left = East), walk 3 km East → (3,−5). Turn right (facing East, right = South), walk 4 km South → (3,−9).
Vector from start to end: (+3,−9) → East + South.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: South-East.

questions.question: In a group of 5 people, who earns the most? Statement I: A earns more than B and C but less than D. Statement II: E earns less than D but more than A.
questions.title: Data sufficiency — who earns the most
options: Only Conclusions I and II follow

sections.label: Given
sections.content: I: A>B, A>C, A<D. II: E<D, E>A.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content: Combining both: D > A > B, C and D > E > A, so D > E > A > B, C — D is above everyone else mentioned in this group of 5 (A,B,C,D,E).

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: D earns the most — **both statements together are needed** (Statement I alone doesn't place E; Statement II alone doesn't place B, C).

questions.question: Which of the following symbols should replace the question marks respectively in the expression "A > B ? C >= D ? E" to ensure that "A > D" and "C > E" are both definitively true?
questions.title: Fill symbols so A>D and C>E are guaranteed

sections.label: Given
sections.content: A > B ? C >= D ? E

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
Fill both blanks with **">"**: A > B > C >= D > E.
- A>B>C gives A>C (strict); combined with C≥D gives A>D (strict transitivity holds when at least one link is strict). ✓
- C≥D>E gives C>E (strict, same reasoning). ✓

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: Both blanks = ">" → "A > B > C >= D > E".

questions.question: A man is facing North-West. He turns 90 degrees in the clockwise direction, then 180 degrees in the anticlockwise direction, and then another 90 degrees in the same direction. Which direction is he facing now?
questions.title: Man facing North-West, series of turns

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: South-East.

questions.question: Introducing someone, Sita says "He is the husband of the granddaughter of the father of my father." How is the man related to Sita?
questions.title: Relationship: "husband of the granddaughter of the father of my father"

sections.label: Steps
sections.content: Father of my father = my paternal grandfather. His granddaughter (in this context) = Sita herself. Husband of that granddaughter = Sita's husband.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: The man is **Sita's husband**.

questions.question: In a certain code, GOAL is written as HPBM and POST is written as QPTU. What is the code for NAME?
questions.title: Coding: GOAL→HPBM, POST→QPTU, find NAME

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
Check the shift: G(7)→H(8) = +1; O(15)→P(16) = +1; A(1)→B(2) = +1; L(12)→M(13) = +1 (confirmed consistently with POST→QPTU too). Every letter shifts forward by exactly 1.
Apply to NAME: N(14)→O(15), A(1)→B(2), M(13)→N(14), E(5)→F(6).

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: OBNF.

questions.question: Statements: All pens are pencils. Some pencils are erasers. No eraser is a scale. Conclusions: I. Some pens are erasers. II. No pen is a scale. III. Some pencils are not scales. Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.title: Syllogism — pens/pencils/erasers/scale
options: Only Conclusions I and II follow

sections.label: Given
sections.content: All pens are pencils. Some pencils are erasers. No eraser is a scale.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content: Conclusion I ("Some pens are erasers") — not guaranteed, since the pencils that are erasers might not overlap with the pencils that are pens. Conclusion II ("No pen is a scale") — not established, since pens' relation to scale is never stated. Conclusion III ("Some pencils are not scales") — since some pencils are erasers, and no eraser is a scale, those particular pencils are definitely not scales, so this follows.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: Only Conclusion III follows.

questions.question: A large solid cube is painted on all its surfaces and then cut into 125 smaller identical cubes. How many of these smaller cubes will have at least two faces painted?
questions.title: Cube painted and cut into 125 smaller cubes — at least 2 faces painted

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
125 = 5³, so it's a 5×5×5 cube. For an n×n×n cube: corner cubes (3 faces painted) = always 8. Edge cubes (exactly 2 faces painted, non-corner) = 12×(n−2) = 12×3 = 36.
At least 2 faces painted = corners + edges = 8 + 36.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: 44 smaller cubes.

questions.question: Statements: Only a few Scripts are Words. No Word is a Letter. All Letters are Alphabets. Conclusions: I. All Scripts being Words is a possibility. II. Some Alphabets are definitely not Words.
questions.title: Syllogism — Scripts/Words/Letters/Alphabets

sections.label: Given
sections.content: Only a few Scripts are Words. No Word is a Letter. All Letters are Alphabets.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content: "Only a few" conventionally means "some, but definitely not all" — so Conclusion I ("All Scripts being Words is a possibility") is already ruled out by the statement itself, so it does NOT follow. Conclusion II: since all Letters are Alphabets, and no Word is a Letter, the Letters (a subset of Alphabets) are definitely not Words — so some Alphabets are definitely not Words. This follows.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: Only Conclusion II follows.

questions.question: Pointing to a man in a photograph, a woman said "His mother's only daughter is my mother." How is the woman related to the man?
questions.title: Relationship: "His mother's only daughter is my mother"

sections.label: Steps
sections.content: "His mother's only daughter" = the man's only sister (since it's a different person from "him," being described in third person). "My mother" = that sister. So the woman's mother is the man's sister.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: The woman is the man's **niece**.

questions.question: Five friends P, Q, R, S, and T are sitting in a straight line facing North. Who sits exactly in the middle? Statement I: R sits third to the right of P, and T sits immediately left of R. Statement II: Q sits second to the left of T, and P is not sitting at any of the extreme ends.
questions.title: Seating puzzle — P, Q, R, S, T in a row, facing North

sections.label: Given
sections.content: I: R is 3rd to the right of P; T is immediately left of R. II: Q is 2nd to the left of T; P is not at an extreme end.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content: From I: R = P+3, T = R−1 = P+2. Two cases: (P=1,T=3,R=4) or (P=2,T=4,R=5). Statement II eliminates P=1 (extreme end), leaving P=2, T=4, R=5. Remaining seats (1 and 3) go to Q and S; working through statement II's placement clue for Q, S lands in the middle seat.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: Using **both statements together**, **S sits in the middle** (seat 3), with the order P(2), T(4), R(5), and Q, S filling seats 1 and 3.

questions.question: Statements: F ? G < H = I; J > H. Conclusions: I. J > F II. I > G. Which of the following is true?
questions.title: Coded inequality — F ? G < H = I; J > H
options: Only Conclusions I and II follow

sections.label: Given
sections.content: Conclusions: I. J > F, II. I > G.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content: The "?" between F and G is an undefined relation, breaking any certain link from F to the rest of the chain (G < H = I < J). So Conclusion I (J > F) cannot be guaranteed. Conclusion II (I > G) doesn't need F at all: I = H and G < H, so G < I directly.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: Only Conclusion II follows.

questions.question: In a certain code language, 123 means 'hot filtered coffee', 356 means 'very hot day' and 589 means 'day and night'. Which digit stands for 'very'?
questions.title: Coded sentence — find the digit for 'very'

sections.label: Given
sections.content: 123='hot filtered coffee', 356='very hot day', 589='day and night'.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
Common word between sentence 1 and 2 is "hot" → common digit between "123" and "356" is **3** → 3 = hot.
Common word between sentence 2 and 3 is "day" → common digit between "356" and "589" is **5** → 5 = day.
In "356" (= very hot day), digits are 3(hot), 5(day), and the remaining digit 6 must represent the remaining word.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: 6 stands for 'very'.

questions.question: Statements: A > B ? C = D < E. Conclusions: I. A > D II. E > B. Which of the following is true?
questions.title: Coded inequality — A>B ? C=D<E

sections.label: Given
sections.content: Conclusions: I. A>D, II. E>B.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content: The "?" between B and C is undefined, breaking the chain in both directions needed. Conclusion I needs to relate A (left of the "?") to D (right of the "?") — blocked. Conclusion II needs to relate E (right of "?") to B (left of "?") — also blocked.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: Neither I nor II follows.

questions.question: If the letters of the word ALGORITHM are arranged in alphabetical order, which letter will be 5th from the left?
questions.title: ALGORITHM in alphabetical order — 5th letter from the left

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
Letters: A, L, G, O, R, I, T, H, M. Sorted alphabetically: A, G, H, I, L, M, O, R, T.
Counting: 1-A, 2-G, 3-H, 4-I, 5-L.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: L.

questions.question: In a certain code language, MYSTIFY is written as NZTUJGZ. How is PROBLEM coded in the same language?
questions.title: Coding: MYSTIFY → NZTUJGZ, find PROBLEM

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
Check the shift: M(13)→N(14)=+1, Y(25)→Z(26)=+1, S(19)→T(20)=+1, T(20)→U(21)=+1, I(9)→J(10)=+1, F(6)→G(7)=+1, Y(25)→Z(26)=+1. A consistent +1 shift on every letter.
Apply to PROBLEM: P→Q, R→S, O→P, B→C, L→M, E→F, M→N.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: QSPCMFN.

questions.question: Statements: W > X = Y ? Z; V < X. Conclusions: I. W > V II. Y > V. Which of the following is true?
questions.title: Coded inequality — W>X=Y ? Z; V<X

sections.label: Given
sections.content: Conclusions: I. W>V, II. Y>V.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content: The "?" is between Y and Z, which is irrelevant to both conclusions. We directly know W>X and V<X (so X>V), giving W>V (Conclusion I: valid). Also Y=X, and X>V, so Y>V (Conclusion II: valid).

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: Both I and II follow.

questions.question: Statements: A ? B > C = D; E < C. Conclusions: I. A > E II. B > D. Which of the following is true?
questions.title: Coded inequality — A ? B>C=D; E<C

sections.label: Given
sections.content: Conclusions: I. A>E, II. B>D.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content: The "?" is between A and B, blocking any certain relation between A and the rest of the chain, so Conclusion I (A>E) doesn't follow. Conclusion II doesn't need A: B>C and C=D directly give B>D.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: Only Conclusion II follows.

questions.question: Eight people are ranked 1 to 8. P is ranked higher than Q but lower than R. S is ranked just below T. T ranks higher than R. U is ranked between Q and V. V is ranked below Q. Who is ranked 4th?
questions.title: Ranking puzzle — 8 people, who is ranked 4th

sections.label: Given
sections.content: R > P > Q (rank order, R best); S is immediately below T; T ranks higher than R; U is between Q and V; V is below Q.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
Order chain: T < R < P < Q < U < V (using rank numbers, 1=best). With T as the topmost defined rank and S = T+1 (immediately below T), assign T=1, S=2. The remaining 6 rank numbers (3–8) are filled by R, P, Q, U, V (in that increasing order) plus one unnamed 8th person taking the last remaining slot.
This gives: 1-T, 2-S, 3-R, 4-P, 5-Q, 6-U, 7-V, 8-(unnamed).

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: P is ranked 4th.

questions.question: If the 3rd of a month falls on Friday, what day will be on the 21st of the same month?
questions.title: Day of the week — 3rd is Friday, what is the 21st?
options: Only Conclusions I and II follow

sections.label: Steps
sections.content: 21 − 3 = 18 days later. 18 mod 7 = 4. Friday + 4 days = Tuesday.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: Tuesday.

questions.question: A clock is set right at 8 AM. The clock gains 10 minutes in 24 hours. What will be the true time when the clock indicates 1 PM on the following day?
questions.title: Clock gaining time — true time when clock shows 1 PM next day

sections.label: Given
sections.content: Clock set right at 8 AM; gains 10 minutes every 24 hours (true time).

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
From 8 AM to 1 PM next day is 29 hours of clock-displayed time = 1740 minutes.
Ratio: clock time : true time = 1450 min : 1440 min (since in 1440 true minutes, the clock shows 1450). So True elapsed = 1740 × (1440/1450) = 1740 × (144/145) = 1728 minutes = 28 hours 48 minutes.
True time = 8 AM + 28h 48m = 8 AM (next day) + 4h 48m.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: 12:48 PM (next day).

questions.question: In a class of 35 students, Priya ranks 8th from the top. Neha is 10 ranks below Priya. What is Neha's rank from the bottom?
questions.title: Class ranking — Priya, Neha

sections.label: Given
sections.content: Class of 35; Priya = 8th from top; Neha is 10 ranks below Priya.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content: Neha's rank from top = 8 + 10 = 18. Rank from bottom = Total − Rank(top) + 1 = 35 − 18 + 1.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: 18th from the bottom.

questions.question: Pointing to a gentleman, Deepak said, "His only brother is the father of my daughter's father." How is the gentleman related to Deepak?
questions.title: Relationship: "His only brother is the father of my daughter's father"

sections.label: Steps
sections.content: "My daughter's father" = Deepak himself (he's the father of his own daughter). "Father of my daughter's father" = Deepak's father. So "His only brother is Deepak's father" → the gentleman's brother is Deepak's father → the gentleman is Deepak's father's brother.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: The gentleman is Deepak's **uncle (paternal uncle)**.

questions.question: Five friends P, Q, R, S, and T are sitting in a row facing North. S is between T and Q. Q is to the immediate left of R. P is to the immediate left of T. Who is sitting in the middle?
questions.title: Seating puzzle — P, Q, R, S, T in a row facing North

sections.label: Given
sections.content: S is between T and Q; Q is immediately left of R; P is immediately left of T.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content: Try arrangement: P, T, S, Q, R (positions 1–5). Check: P immediately left of T ✓ (1,2). Q immediately left of R ✓ (4,5). S(3) is between T(2) and Q(4) ✓.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **S sits in the middle** (arrangement: P, T, S, Q, R).

questions.question: Prakash walks 30 m towards West, takes a left turn and walks 20 m. He again takes a left turn and walks 30 m. He then takes a right turn and stops. Towards which direction is he facing now?
questions.title: Prakash's walk — final facing direction
options: Only Conclusions I and II follow

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: South.

questions.question: Statements: No software is hardware. All hardware is firmware. Some firmware is malware. Conclusions: I. No software is firmware. II. Some malware is hardware. III. Some firmware is not software. Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.title: Syllogism — software/hardware/firmware/malware

sections.label: Given
sections.content: No software is hardware. All hardware is firmware. Some firmware is malware.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content: Conclusion I ("No software is firmware") — not established, since software's relation to the rest of firmware (beyond hardware) is unknown. Conclusion II ("Some malware is hardware") — not guaranteed, since the firmware-malware overlap isn't confirmed to include hardware specifically. Conclusion III ("Some firmware is not software") — since hardware ⊆ firmware and no software is hardware, that hardware-portion of firmware is definitely not software.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: Only Conclusion III follows.

questions.question: Statements: Some cats are dogs. All dogs are birds. No bird is a fish. Conclusions: I. Some cats are birds. II. No dog is a fish. III. No cat is a fish. Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.title: Syllogism — cats/dogs/birds/fish
options: Only Conclusions I and II follow
questions.answer: Only Conclusions I and II follow

sections.label: Given
sections.content: Some cats are dogs. All dogs are birds. No bird is a fish.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content: Conclusion I ("Some cats are birds") — since some cats are dogs, and all dogs are birds, those cat-dogs are birds → follows. Conclusion II ("No dog is a fish") — all dogs are birds, no bird is fish → no dog is fish → follows. Conclusion III ("No cat is a fish") — only established for the cats that are dogs; other cats' relation to fish is unknown → does not follow.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: Only Conclusions I and II follow.

questions.question: Blood relation: Pointing to a photograph, a man says, 'She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son.' How is the woman related to the man?
questions.title: Blood relation: Pointing to a photograph, a man says, 'She i
options: She is his sister (or himself, but since 'she' is used, she is his sister)
questions.answer: She is his sister (or himself, but since 'she' is used, she is his sister)

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: 'My grandfather's only son' = the man's father (assuming the man's father is an only child of the grandfather) — OR could be the man himself if he is the only son of his grandfather's line.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: Since 'my grandfather's only son' most commonly refers to the speaker's own father (assuming the speaker is not the only son in question), the daughter of that son is the speaker's **sister**.

questions.question: Series: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ? — find the next number.
questions.title: Series: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ? — find the next number.

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: Check the pattern of differences between consecutive terms.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
Differences: 6−2=4, 12−6=6, 20−12=8, 30−20=10 → differences increase by 2 each time. Next difference = 12.
30 + 12 = 42.

questions.question: Coding: If 'RAIN' is coded as 'SBJO', how is 'SNOW' coded?
questions.title: Coding: If 'RAIN' is coded as 'SBJO', how is 'SNOW' coded?

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: Check the shift: R→S(+1), A→B(+1), I→J(+1), N→O(+1) — each letter shifts forward by 1.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content: Apply +1 to SNOW: S→T, N→O, O→P, W→X.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **TOPX.**
